title: Block motif — twelve round
subtitle: A chunky 22 cm solid square block worked to twelve rounds in aran weight
excerpt: Twelve rounds in aran cotton produce a 22 cm solid square — large enough for a standalone dishcloth, a coaster set worked as one piece, or a bold patchwork panel. The construction uses the same four-corner-cluster method throughout; twelve rounds is the natural stopping point before the motif becomes unwieldy.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 1 (1885). Extended block construction.
heroPrompt: A twelve-round solid block crochet motif in natural oatmeal aran cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Dense treble sides, sharp chain-2 corners, 22 cm square.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished block measures 22 × 22 cm in aran-weight cotton with a 5 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Block motif — twelve round
chartDefinition.caption: Twelve rounds from the magic ring. Chain-2 corners; solid treble sides growing by 3 per round.

glossaryTerms.definition: A solid square motif worked to twelve rounds, giving a 22 cm tile suitable for standalone projects or as a large-grid element in blankets.

content.text: reaches 22 cm in aran weight — the largest practical size for a joined-motif block before the piece becomes heavier than the project needs. At this size, four blocks make a 44 cm baby blanket; one block makes a dishcloth or table mat.

Start each round with a sl st into the corner ch-2 space. The ch-3 turning chain and 2 tr into the corner, followed by ch 2 and 3 tr into the same corner, is the same corner formula from round 1 onward. Count the side trebles after each round — they should grow by exactly 3 per side.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 60 g of aran-weight cotton. A 5 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Work rounds 1–8 as per the eight-round block pattern. Continue through rounds 9–12 with the same formula: corner clusters of 3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr and solid trebles into every side stitch. Side treble counts: Rnd 9 = 24; Rnd 10 = 27; Rnd 11 = 30; Rnd 12 = 33.
For a textured version of the large block, try the bavarian crochet square which adds front-post treble ridges around each concentric round.
